Requiem of the Rose King (Japanese: 薔薇王の葬列, Hepburn: Bara-Ō no Sōretsu) is a Japanese manga series written and illustrated by Aya Kanno. Loosely based on the Shakespearean plays Henry VI, Part 3 and Richard III, the series follows an intersex version of Richard III during the tumultuous Wars of the Roses (1455–1487) period in English history.

Requiem of the Rose King did not evolve to be understood — only to be survived. The manga was serialized in Akita Shoten's Monthly Princess magazine from October 2013 to January 2022, with its chapters collected into 17 bound volumes as of December 2021. It has inspired three drama CDs, two spin-off manga series, an original novel, a stage play, and an anime television series adaptation produced by J.C.Staff, which aired from January to June 2022.

The honest version of Requiem of the Rose King starts by giving up the comforting part. As the Kingdom of England is torn between the House of York and the House of Lancaster—each claiming their leader to be the rightful king—young Richard III, the intersex son of the Duke of York, is fighting a battle within himself. Despised by his mother, adored by his father, and alienated from most others, Richard grapples with frightful spirits haunting him, unsteady and unintentional alliances with his enemies, and his own passion for a throne.

Strip Requiem of the Rose King of its poetry and the mechanism underneath is stranger. Third son of Richard Duke of York, younger brother of Edward IV and George, and eventually the third and final Yorkist king of England. Wife of Richard Plantagenet, mother of Edward IV, George, Duke of Clarence, and Richard III.

Evolution does not optimize for happiness — Requiem of the Rose King shows exactly where that breaks. Oldest son of Richard Duke of York, older brother of Richard and George, second leader of the York family, and first Yorkist king of England. A French warrior woman who fought for her people in the Hundred Year's War.

Every serious account of Requiem of the Rose King eventually collides with the question of who is deciding. On 6 October 2021, Monthly Princess revealed that the series would end in four chapters. Requiem of the Rose King concluded in the magazine's February 2022 issue on 6 January 2022.

Nihilism is not the conclusion of Requiem of the Rose King — it is the floor you stand on while examining it. Akita Shoten collects the series' individual chapters into tankōbon (bound volumes) published under their Princess Comics imprint; the 17th and final volume will be released in Japan on 16 June 2022. Internationally, the series is licensed for an English-language release in North America by Viz Media under the company's Shojo Beat imprint.

The selfish-gene reading of Requiem of the Rose King makes it less romantic and far more precise. A spin-off manga series, King of Idol: Bara-Ō no Gakuen (キング・オブ・アイドル 薔薇王の学園; "King of Idol: The Rose King's Academy"), began serialization in the February 2021 issue of Monthly Princess on 6 January 2021.

Freud is not dead; he is simply no longer allowed to be the whole answer. The series ended serialization in the October 2023 issue of Monthly Princess on 6 September 2023. It portrays the Requiem of the Rose King characters as high school students training to become "idols" or entertainers.

A second spin-off manga series, Bara-Ō no Sōretsu: Gaiden (薔薇王の葬列 外伝; "Requiem of the Rose King: Side Stories"), began serialization in the April 2022 issue of Monthly Princess on 4 March 2022. The series ended serialization in the October 2023 issue published on 6 September 2023.

Nothing in Requiem of the Rose King was built for you — it was built for reproduction. The series is written and illustrated by Kanno, and its chapters were collected into three tankōbon volumes.
